page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU Intel Xeon 8581C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration maps 16 vCPUs to 8 physical cores at 2.3 GHz with 2 threads per core, supported by 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It provides 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector acceleration is enabled via AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), covering amx_tile and amx_int8 instruction sets. The server includes no bundled local storage, no discrete GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard cloud networking.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-threaded performance. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0 and a text processing score of 3077.0, both placing in the top 10 percent tier. Single-threaded data throughput is strong, generating 34.81 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.9 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Small language model text generation achieves 336.56 tokens per second, benefiting from hardware matrix acceleration. In contrast, multi-core metrics fall into the median range, with a PassMark CPU score of 23019.02, a multi-core Geekbench score of 13758.0, and Redis SET throughput of 24.68 million operations per second.

The architectural tradeoff centers on core compute speed over memory footprint and bundled persistence. With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and no local NVMe storage, qualitative cost efficiency is highest for compute-bound tasks that do not maintain extensive in-memory state. The hardware profile is appropriate for CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving, high-throughput text processing, batch compression tasks, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-16 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores and 32.0 GB of RAM. Running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor integrates a 260 MB L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates upper-decile single-core efficiency, reaching top-tier results in Geekbench single-core computation, text processing, and lightweight model token generation. Multi-threaded throughput, including clang compilation and database operations, remains near benchmark averages. The configuration lacks bundled local storage, discrete GPUs, and complimentary IPv4 connectivity, yielding a lean 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cost efficiency is maximized when running tasks that fully leverage per-core execution speeds rather than extensive memory arrays. Appropriate workloads include CI/CD build environments, batch compression jobs, static web serving, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
